Kengeri, Bengaluru · Registered Trust

From a sapling
to a tree in full bloom.

Nurturing the pupil since 1957.

What began as a single high school with twenty-five students, run out of a borrowed dharmashala, has grown into a full educational trust — a nursery, a primary school, a high school, a pre-university college and a first-grade college, all serving the families of Kengeri.

Our Story

A trust built by a rural community, for a rural community

In the early 1950s there was no high school within twenty-five kilometres of Kengeri. Every stage of the trust's growth answered the next gap that appeared.

1956

The Kengeri Educational Society is formed

A group of philanthropic residents seeks the Government of Mysore's permission to open a high school for the children of poor farmers, who had no access to schooling beyond the primary level.

1957

Kengeri High School opens its doors

On 6 June 1957, classes begin at Sri Seetharama Dharmashala with a mere 20 to 25 students. A dedicated school building follows in 1970–71 as enrolment grows.

1970–71

Kengeri Pre-University College is started

To spare students the impossible journey into Bengaluru city, the trust opens a PU college with Arts and Science combinations; Commerce is added in the 1980s.

1983

Renamed the Kengeri Educational Trust

The founding society is reconstituted as a registered trust, formalising decades of voluntary service by its honorary trustees.

1994

Kengeri First Grade College is founded

A degree college is added so students can graduate without leaving Kengeri, offering Arts and Commerce combinations to begin with.

Today

Five institutions, one campus community

Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru Nursery School, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru Higher Primary School, Kengeri High School, Kengeri Pre-University College and Kengeri First Grade College now share a ten-acre campus opposite Kengeri Police Station.

About the school

The trust's primary wing carries students through their foundational years in both Kannada and English medium, feeding directly into Kengeri High School next door. As part of the same ten-acre KET campus, pupils share the trust's playgrounds, RO drinking water and CCTV-monitored grounds from their very first year of school.
